extracted.intended_audience: researchers worldwide holding a doctoral-level degree or equivalent (with special emphasis on early-career / young scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a preliminary (and, if invited, full) research proposal to the John Templeton Foundation's Science of Purpose Funding Initiative focused on goal-directed/ purposive phenomena in nature. Applicants should align projects with the initiative's thematic strands and follow the per-strand application forms and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding priority — novel concepts for goal-directed phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation seeks to identify and fund the development of novel theoretical, philosophical, or scientific concepts useful for advancing the study of goal-directed, goal-seeking, or goal-suited phenomena in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should develop new concepts (theoretical, philosophical, or scientific) that advance the study of purposive phenomena; the initiative spans multiple disciplines from chemistry to the biological sciences. The Foundation has allocated over $20 million to this funding priority over the next five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research relevance — focus on purposive categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should attend to purposive categories such as goal-directedness, agency, and directionality as useful or necessary for scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should explain how greater attentiveness to categories like goal-directedness, agency, or directionality will catalyze novel theory development or scientific discoveries in areas such as AI, origin of life, development, macroevolution trends, ecology, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each strand link opens a unique set of questions illustrative of the kinds of concepts or phenomena the funding priority seeks to support; each strand page contains an application form with specific submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Commonalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonalities is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See per-strand link for specific questions and application form/instructions; used to indicate topical fit for proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Development is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the Development strand link for the particular questions and application form relevant to this topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Life
rubrics_metrics.description: Life is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects concerning life and purposive phenomena should be mapped to this strand and follow its application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Macroevolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Macroevolution is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals addressing macroevolutionary patterns related to purposiveness should use the Macroevolution strand link and application form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants whose work is about physical/material aspects of purposive phenomena should consult the Matter strand page for guidance and application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanistic studies of goal-directed phenomena should follow the Mechanisms strand's questions and application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Models
rubrics_metrics.description: Models is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Models strand is the appropriate topical fit for theoretical or computational modeling proposals; see its application form for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strand: Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization is one of nine strands of research applicants are encouraged to explore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects about organizational principles of purposive systems should use the Organization strand link and application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process — two-stage application
rubrics_metrics.description: The initiative has a two-stage funding process: submit a preliminary application as stage one; successful preliminary applicants will be invited to submit a full proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each strand link contains an application form with specific submission instructions. Applicants are encouraged to submit as many project ideas as are of interest. All applicants will be notified of the outcome of their initial application by November 30 using the email provided. Successful applicants will be invited to submit a full proposal to the Foundation no later than February 1, 2021. Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their full proposal review and decisioning by June 21, 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process — panel composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will be reviewed by a panel of referees comprised of scientists and philosophers and Foundation staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection from the preliminary stage is determined by this review panel; invited applicants proceed to submit a full proposal per the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — doctoral-level researchers; emphasis on young scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: This funding competition is open to researchers worldwide who hold a doctoral-level degree or equivalent at the time of application. Special emphasis is given to young scholars at this stage of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous entrants to the Templeton Ideas Challenge may apply; if applicants cannot find a fitting strand, they are invited to submit a proposed project via the provided link. For questions, contact purpose@templeton.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application guidance — submit multiple ideas / propose new topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to submit as many project ideas as are of interest. If a research topic does not fit the listed strands, applicants may submit a proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the per-strand application forms and follow their specific instructions; the initiative is flexible about topical fit so long as projects align with the funding priority on purposive phenomena.
